Workers and beat scheduler now depend only on network-online.target and redis-server.service, properly treating them as independent services.

findings.detail: Both infra/systemd/juli-celery-worker.service and juli-celery-beat.service created following juli-api.service pattern (ExecStartPre, EnvironmentFile, WorkingDirectory, Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5)
Celery command references correct module path (juli_backend.workers.celery_app) verified against actual codebase
Beat scheduler does not hardcode schedule; relies entirely on celery_app.py's existing beat_schedule dict (verified)

docs/runbooks/app-review-runbook.md correctly integrates new units: added redis-server to Step 1 package list, added two new 'sudo cp' lines in Step 4, added two rows to config files table, added journalctl examples to log section
infra/scripts/env/api.env.example guidance updated from 'leave unset' to actionable uncomment instructions with reference to Issue #720
Scope containment verified: no changes to backend/src/juli_backend/, deploy-release.sh, release.yml, or test files; forbidden-token test list not modified
Acceptance commands pass: 18/18 tests in test_phase_2_5_deploy_config.py, ruff check passes

BindsTo=juli-api.service removed from both units. Handoff explicitly states 'follow juli-api.service's exact pattern'; juli-api.service uses only After= and Wants=, never BindsTo. BindsTo would create asymmetric coupling where API restart kills workers (wrong). Workers must be independent services depending on network and redis only.

convention_notes.standard: systemd best practices for multiple related services
convention_notes.note: Correct use of After= for ordering, Wants= for soft dependency, removal of BindsTo to maintain service independence. Multi-user.target in WantedBy is standard for user-space services.

Units follow juli-api.service pattern exactly: root user, /root/releases/current working dir, ExecStartPre secret fetch, EnvironmentFile from stable /etc/juli path outside release tree, Type=simple, Restart=on-failure with RestartSec=5

verdict: Spec fidelity: PASS. Corrected improper BindsTo dependency that violated pattern-follow requirement; all other acceptance criteria met. Ready for Guardrails phase.
